'''Matsura-gun''' is a historical [[Commandery (China)|county]] in Japan. It was located in [[Hizen Province]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Yoshida |first=Keiichi |date=1968 |title=A Historico-geographical Study of Western Part of Matsuura-gun in Hizen Province |url=https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jjhg1948/20/5/20_5_570/_article |journal=Japanese Journal of Human Geography |volume=20 |issue=5 |pages=570–586 |doi=10.4200/jjhg1948.20.570|doi-access=free }}</ref>

The Matsura region, [[Matsura Sayohime|Sayohime's]] alluded place of origin, spans the current-day Nagasaki and [[Saga Prefecture]]s.{{sfnp|Kimbrough|2013|p=60}} However, the specific mountaintop that had been dubbed {{nihongo|Hirefurinomine|領巾麾嶺|extra="Scarf-Waving Peak"}}, as attested in the ''Man'yōshū'',{{sfnp|Nagano|1974|p=1}} has been identified as the summit of {{interlanguage link|Mount Kagami (Saga)|lt=Mount Kagami|ja|鏡山 (佐賀県)}}, on the eastern edge of the city of [[Karatsu, Saga]].{{Refn|Japanese sources state the mountain overlooks Karatsu Bay ({{interlanguage link|Karatsu wan|ja|唐津湾}}),<ref name=daijiten-hirefurinomine/> whereas Cranston says there is a view to "Matsura Bay".<ref name="Cranston"/> It is not entirely clear whether he meant {{nihongo|Matsura-gata|松浦潟}} on the current map (a "lagoon" which is part of Karatsu Bay), or the old name {{nihongo|Matsura-wan|松浦湾}} which is somewhat ambiguous.|group="lower-alpha"}}

Some versions of the legend of [[Matsura Sayohime]](var. Lady Otohi or Otohi-hime) are classed as the {{nihongo|''Miwasan-kei setsuwa''|三輪山型説話|extra="stories of the Mt. Miwa pattern"}}{{Refn|Cranston remarks that a myth similar to the "Grave of Chopstick" myth above (his tale 122) has been interpolated, but other scholars prefer to compare the Lady Otohi legend to "The Mt. Miwa Story" because they both share the motif of the lady attaching a thread to her husband to discover his true identity to be a snake.<ref name=nagano/> Kelsey does not categorize this as a god-husband tale (i.e., pp. 219, 232), listing it instead among the "Violent Deities", subtype "IV. Sexual Violence", p. 231.|group="lower-alpha"}} But there is no enduring sign of snake worship in the original vicinity of the legend in the Matsura region, where a local shrine houses the supposed petrified remains, or {{nihongo|''bōfuseki''|望夫石|extra="rock that contemplates the husband"}}, of Lady Matsura.{{efn|Sayohime Shrine, part of [[Tashima Shrine]].}}

[[Kagami Shrine]] was the main shrine and [[Soja shrine]] of Matsura-gun{{Citation needed|date=October 2023}}
